principles: Preserve CLI observable behavior while reducing file-level concentration.
Separate command catalog, parsing/help, runtime gates, and lifecycle orchestration before moving handlers.
Keep process facts and Authority evidence mechanically verifiable rather than prose-only.
Make each implementation slice small enough to review, revert, and validate independently.
drivers: cli-engine.ts has grown into a high-risk god file.
Command schema and gate behavior are process-critical and test-facing.
The user requested documentation first and strong Authority verification for this major architecture change.

options.name: A: Write a staged execution plan first, then split implementation into reviewed stories
pros: Keeps B-0717 documentation-only and avoids accidental behavior changes.
Allows Authority receipt requirements and 3x2 host quorum to be defined before implementation.
Lets later stories preserve compatibility re-exports while shrinking cli-engine.ts incrementally.
cons: Does not immediately reduce the cli-engine.ts line count.
Requires follow-up implementation stories to realize the plan.

options.name: B: Refactor cli-engine.ts immediately inside this story
pros: Would start reducing the file now.
cons: Violates the user request to write the document first.
Combines planning, Authority validation, and code migration in one high-risk change.
Makes rollback and review boundaries unclear.

options.name: C: Only record a short backlog note
cons: Does not define Authority Server receipt flow, 3x2 quorum, or implementation slices.
Would leave future hosts guessing at contracts and stop conditions.

chosen: A: Write a staged execution plan first, then split implementation into reviewed stories
rationale: Choose the staged execution plan because the requested work is a major architecture decomposition with process-gate and Authority implications; implementation should only begin after the plan fixes module boundaries, compatibility contracts, receipt semantics, review quorum, and rollback conditions.

preMortem.scenario: Plan accidentally authorizes behavior changes in B-0717
preMortem.trigger: The document mixes planning with direct refactor instructions for the current story.
preMortem.consequence: Review evidence becomes misleading and the user loses the clean planning boundary.
preMortem.mitigation: State B-0717 is documentation/readiness only and list source refactors as future stories.

preMortem.trigger: Local authority_status or local verdict storage is described as production Authority completion.
preMortem.consequence: DONE evidence could imply a server-backed receipt that does not exist.
preMortem.mitigation: Require authority_receipt_verify with a production gate_decision receipt for Authority completion; classify local 3x2 as lower-assurance when Authority is off.

preMortem.scenario: Future implementation breaks CLI contract imports
preMortem.trigger: Symbols imported from cli-engine.ts are moved without re-export or test migration.
preMortem.consequence: Tests, scripts, or downstream callers fail after decomposition.
preMortem.mitigation: Document exported compatibility surface and require build plus process/command ownership contract tests after each slice.

preMortem.scenario: The split creates many tiny modules without reducing risk
preMortem.trigger: The plan follows line-count goals instead of responsibility boundaries.
preMortem.consequence: Complexity moves around and reviewers cannot reason about lifecycle gates.
preMortem.mitigation: Organize slices by command catalog, parsing/help, runtime gates, and lifecycle special dispatchers with specific verification gates.
